Subject: Security & KMS: post-demo follow-up and vendor questionnaire

Hi Alice / Bob —

Thanks again for the time today — really helpful to understand FinBank's latency and compliance needs for the payments fraud use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of ask:
- You need SOC 2 Type II evidence and confirmation of data residency (US-only) for production.
- You asked about GDPR/HIPAA applicability for PII in prompts/outputs.
- KMS: preference for customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) with HSM-backed KMS and key rotation controls; clarity on at-rest vs in-transit encryption.

What we can provide / initial answers:
- SOC 2: Redwood has a current SOC 2 Type II report; we can share the redacted report under an NDA or via your secure portal.
- GDPR/HIPAA: We support data processing addenda and can discuss a tailored DPA; HIPAA support available under enterprise agreements with BAAs for covered workloads.
- Encryption: All customer data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+). At rest, model weights and customer prompt/response data are encrypted using AES-256. We support customer-managed keys via integrations with AWS KMS and external HSM providers for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Open items / asks from FinBank:
1) Please start the vendor security questionnaire (attached) and flag any high-priority items so we can route to the right teams.
2) Confirm whether you require customer-managed keys for dev/test or only prod.
3) Confirm required timeline for SOC 2 evidence and whether you have a portal (e.g., SecureDocs) we should upload to.

Next steps I propose:
- I'll attach a short KMS architecture diagram and a starter answers doc for the VSQ. Rishi (cc) will provide a few technical answers about HSM support. David (cc) will follow up on SOC 2 upload.
- If helpful, let's schedule a 30-min follow-up with your security team next week (I'm available Wed/Thu morning PST).

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Best,

Marissa Cole

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and for the attachments. A couple of clarifying questions from our side: 

1) Customer-managed keys: we need to understand the deployment models that support BYOK. Specifically, does Redwood support: 
   - fully customer-managed HSM (on-prem HSM + Redwood Private)
   - customer-managed KMS in cloud (our AWS KMS keys in our account) with Redwood accessing via cross-account grants
   - Bring-your-own-key for Hosted API (we understand this may be limited)

2) HSM vs KMS: do you support FIPS 140-2 level 3 HSMs for key storage or only cloud KMS (AWS KMS/EKMS) with HSM backing? We have a compliance requirement to prefer HSM-backed keys with attestations.

3) Soc 2: we need the latest Type II report and the date range covered. Can the report be shared via SecureDocs or uploaded to our procurement portal?

4) Timeline: we are aiming to complete vendor assessments within the next 3 weeks — can your security/compliance and infra teams respond within that window?

Also — we'll start the questionnaire and send an initial batch by EOD. Can you confirm who on your side will own the VSQ responses?

Thanks,

Alice Turner

Subject: Re: Security & KMS: post-demo follow-up and vendor questionnaire

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the questions — answering inline for clarity: 

> 1) Customer-managed keys: we need to understand the deployment models that support BYOK. Specifically, does Redwood support: 
>    - fully customer-managed HSM (on-prem HSM + Redwood Private)
>    - customer-managed KMS in cloud (our AWS KMS keys in our account) with Redwood accessing via cross-account grants
>    - Bring-your-own-key for Hosted API (we understand this may be limited)

- Short answer: We support all three models but with different tradeoffs and availability: 
  - Redwood Private (on-prem or VPC with Private control plane) can integrate with an on-prem HSM cluster — customers can present keys via our KMIP or HSM-native connectors; this is our recommended path for customers requiring dedicated HSMs and FIPS 140-2 L3 attestations.
  - For cloud deployments (Dedicated), we support customer-managed keys in your cloud account (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) via cross-account roles/grants. Keys remain in your account; Redwood services are granted decrypt/encrypt ability scoped to the key.
  - For Hosted API: BYOK is supported via Bring-Your-Own-Key partners in limited cases (enterprise-only, must be preconfigured) — most customers use envelope encryption where we hold a service key and you control a wrapping key in your KMS.

> 2) HSM vs KMS: do you support FIPS 140-2 level 3 HSMs for key storage or only cloud KMS (AWS KMS/EKMS) with HSM backing?

- We can support FIPS 140-2 L3 HSMs for Private deployments with on-prem HSMs; for Dedicated (cloud-hosted), we rely on cloud provider KMS which is HSM-backed (AWS KMS, CloudHSM integration available) and we can provide attestation artifacts where available.

> 3) Soc 2: we need the latest Type II report and the date range covered. Can the report be shared via SecureDocs or uploaded to our procurement portal?

- David (cc) owns compliance artifacts. We can upload to SecureDocs or your portal; our current SOC 2 Type II covers 2025-07-01 through 2026-06-30 (redacted copy available).

> 4) Timeline: we are aiming to complete vendor assessments within the next 3 weeks — can your security/compliance and infra teams respond within that window?

- We can meet that timeline for the initial VSQ answers and SOC 2 upload. For deeper architecture reviews or HSM integration testing, we may need an additional week depending on scheduling.

Who owns VSQ: I'll take point on the technical sections, Marissa will own procurement/contacts, and David will handle SOC 2 and attestation artifacts.

Let me know if you want a short write-up of the envelope encryption flow (we have a diagram attached).

Thanks,

Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Applied ML Engineer, Security Integrations
